div.head: Episc 1
div.ab: Episcopo (iure) pertinet, omne rectum (omnem rectitudinem) promovere, Dei uidelicet et (ac) seculi.
Bisceope gebyreð ælc rihting, ge on godcundan þingan ge on woruldcundan.
Item Bisceope gebyreð ælc rihting, ge on godcundan þingan ge on woruldcundan.
It is proper for a bishop to offer guidance in all things, both in religious and secular matters.
Einem Bischofe gebührt jede Leitung sowohl in kirchlichen Dingen wie in weltlichen.
To a bishop belongs all direction, both in spiritual matters and in secular ones.
div.note: Spacing and a line break inside K were tidied.
Manuscripts: X = Oxford, Bodleian Library, MS Junius 121, fols. 13v–15r. Item: preceded by vii. in manuscript

[title] Furthermore: This is the only title given to the text in the manuscript, where it follows the sixth chapter of 2 Polity (“Likewise, Concerning Bishops”). The title Episcopus (On Episcopal Duties) was given to it by Liebermann.
